title: Exclusive: AI startup Chai lands GSK deal, its sixth pharma partner in nine months
source_used: Contract Pharma (carrying Chai Discovery's announcement); Endpoints News (headline only, paywalled)
key_facts: Chai Discovery, an AI company building a computer-aided design suite for molecules, announced a collaboration with drugmaker GSK.
The agreement follows a technology evaluation in which GSK ran internal wet-lab (laboratory) tests of Chai's designs.
Chai generated the designs for GSK targets without target-specific training (zero-shot); Chai says GSK found binders to all tested targets.
GSK gains access to Chai's platform, including its protein folding and design models, for drug discovery.
Christopher Austin, GSK's senior vice president of R&D technologies, said GSK 'saw designs with strong binding affinities'.
Chai's latest model is called Chai-3; the company says it reaches high target success rates and binding affinities.
The Endpoints News headline calls it Chai's sixth pharma partner in nine months (article body paywalled).
quote_evidence: GSK found binders to all tested targets—resulting in the expansion of its work with Chai into a broader collaboration.
“We evaluated their models across a panel of diverse targets and saw designs with strong binding affinities.”
Since the start of 2026, Chai says it has entered into numerous partnerships with leading pharmaceutical companies.
why_it_matters_hint: Drugmakers are testing AI molecule-design tools in their own labs before signing deals.
notes: Endpoints News exclusive is paywalled (only headline and first lines seen); Fierce Biotech and Business Wire were blocked. Facts come from Contract Pharma's write-up of the Chai announcement. Results are the companies' own statements.
